title: nazm.test-summary/1
description: One `nazm test` run, compactly, from `nazm test --summary-json`: its outcome and exit status, counts from each case's own verdict, and every case that did not pass with how each leg ended — no passed names, no program output. An additive view, not a replacement: `nazm test --json` still gives every case in full as `nazm.test/1`. No timing, timestamp or host path beyond each case's file as named is included.

status.description: `passed`: every case passed. `failed`: at least one did not. `no_cases`: no `.nz` beside a `.expected` was found — refused, as the command refuses it. `unreadable`: a named path is not a file or a directory. `toolchain_failed`: the runner could not find itself or make its working directory.

exit_code.description: The process exit status, exactly as without `--summary-json`.

native.description: Whether each case also ran as a compiled executable; false with `--interpret-only`.

passed.description: Cases whose own verdict is passed — counted, never `cases` minus `failed`.

without_expectation.description: `.nz` files with no `.expected` beside them: not cases, counted rather than listed.

name.description: As `nazm.test/1` names the case: the file's stem, which two directories may share.

file.description: As `nazm.test/1` gives it: the path as named on the command line or found in a directory. The case's identity.

failures.description: Every case that did not pass, in the order the cases ran — the order named and, within a directory, sorted — never completion order. Not truncated.

leg.description: How one leg ended, from what the runner did — never from output text. `mismatched`: it ran and its output was not the recorded one, which includes a runtime error or a diagnostic in that output; no diagnostic is inferred from it. `not_run`: `--interpret-only`. `build_failed`: `nazm build` ran and did not succeed. `could_not_build`, `could_not_run`: the process could not be started.
